children: Hungary's central bank will decide on the future path of interest rates based on its September inflation projection, it said on Thursday, in response to questions about a Bloomberg report saying the bank would pause rate easing this month.

Citing a source familiar with the matter, Bloomberg said the bank would pause rate cuts at 5.5% at its September 22 policy meeting as it prepares to lower its 3% inflation target to 2.5% - part of Hungary's efforts to join the euro.

"As Governor Mihaly Varga indicated following the Monetary Council's interest rate-setting meeting on 25 August 2026, the Council will decide on the future path of the base rate on the basis of the September Inflation Report," the bank said.
"The review of the inflation target is currently underway, and the central bank will provide information on the outcome during the autumn," it said in response to emailed questions.

Last month the bank delivered its third successive quarter-point rate cut, as expected, to 5.5%, and left the door open to further rate easing depending on its September inflation projections and global market developments.
Economists polled by Reuters before that meeting projected 50 basis points worth of additional rate cuts to 5% by the end of this year.

Hungary's inflation, which scaled the European Union's highest levels following Russia's February 2022 invasion of neighbouring Ukraine, plunged to an annual 1.2% in July, its lowest in almost a decade.

Deputy Governor Zoltan Kurali told Reuters in June that the bank's inflation target review would examine the impact of a lower target closer to euro zone levels, and the strategy and timing for any change, which could come in one or two steps.
